mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the federal funds rate above 5.0% signals a tightening monetary policy regime that increases discount rates on future equity cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS exceeds 5.0%, or the average return in triggered periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate below 4.5% signals tightening labor market conditions that increase wage pressures and inflation expectations, prompting central bank hawkishness and reducing equity valuations over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX generates positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of cases when UNRATE falls below 4.5%, or the mean return in such periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in residential construction starts above 1.6 million units signals strong household demand and rising inflationary pressures, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX delivers positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when HOUST exceeds 1600.0, or the average return in such periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in industrial production below 110.0 indicates weakening manufacturing activity and a contraction in real output, which triggers market expectations of economic slowdown and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as equities reprice for lower growth and potential policy easing.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO falls below 110.0, or the average return in such periods is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in both real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) signals strong aggregate demand and rising inflation expectations, which increases the probability of a Fed rate hike and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX generates positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of cases where both RSAFS and HOUST are rising, or the joint signal fails to produce a statistically significant negative return (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the CPIAUCSL above 202.5 combined with a stable FEDFUNDS rate signals persistent inflationary pressure without policy response, increasing the risk of future rate hikes and leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX delivers positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL exceeds 202.5 and FEDFUNDS is stable, or the joint signal does not produce a significant negative return (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) and a decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strong labor market that fuels wage growth and inflation, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to heightened expectations of monetary tightening.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of cases where PAYEMS rises and UNRATE falls, or the joint signal fails to generate a statistically significant negative return (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained expansion in real GDP (GDPC1) above 11540 billion dollars combined with rising residential construction (HOUST) indicates strong economic momentum and rising inflation expectations, which increases the likelihood of Fed tightening and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX delivers positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances when both GDPC1 and HOUST are rising, or the joint signal does not produce a significant negative return (t-test p > 0.05).
